setlist.title: It's All Over Now, Baby Blue

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **It's All Over Now, Baby Blue** (2 reviews): Listener rates this specific song performance as great; Performer plays a nice slow version of this song [3][5]
- **China Cat Sunflower** (2 reviews): Listener claims this is the hardest rocking China Cat available; Song drops off without much of a jam into High Time [9][10]
- **The Eleven** (1 review): Song is cut off after Jerry flubbed key phrases [10]
- **Casey Jones** (1 review): This performance is described as really a prototype [10]
- **Turn on Your Lovelight** (1 review): This track is described as raw and tight [6]

## The recordings

- **gd69-07-05.sbd.cotsman.4282.sbefail.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 11 songs; 116 min; rated 3/5 by 10 [1]. Said about its sound: Recording is muddy with significant hiss, though performance quality is high; Audio quality is poor through the first half of the recording; Tape hiss is apparent during low dynamics; tape wobble affects Baby Blue [2][3][5][8]

## Around the show

- Venue sounds almost empty, creating a hollow acoustic effect [6]
- Band enthusiastically searches for sound in Chicago's Electric Theater [9]
- First couple songs are good, but the rest is shaky [7]
- Dark Star here is 18 minutes, unlike the short 4/26 version [8]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd69-07-05.sbd.cotsman.4282.sbefail.shnf**: source: Soundboard [1]. Also: Beginning of Morning Dew is clipped; quality improves into the song; Minor splice occurs during the first few notes of Baby Blue; Volume fluctuations were adjusted using Sound Forge software [1]
